# Proverbs 21 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The LORD directs a king's heart as easily as redirecting a stream of water — He moves it wherever He wants.

**2** People always think they're doing the right thing, but the LORD examines what's really in their hearts.

**3** Doing what's right and fair matters more to the LORD than any religious ritual.

**4** Proud looks and an arrogant heart — everything about the wicked is sinful.

**5** Careful planning by hard workers leads to plenty, but rushing leads to poverty.

**6** Wealth gained through lies is a disappearing mist — a death trap for those who chase it.

**7** The violence of the wicked drags them down, because they refuse to do what's right.

**8** A guilty person's path is twisted, but a clean person's actions are straightforward.

**9** Better to live in the corner of a rooftop than share an entire house with a nagging spouse.

**10** A wicked person craves doing harm — they show no mercy even to their own neighbors.

**11** Punish a mocker and inexperienced people learn. Teach a wise person and they absorb even more.

**12** The Righteous God watches the household of the wicked and eventually brings them to ruin.

**13** If you plug your ears when poor people cry for help, don't be surprised when you cry out and nobody answers.

**14** A quiet gift calms anger, and a secret offering soothes intense rage.

**15** When justice is served, the righteous celebrate — but the wicked are terrified.

**16** Anyone who wanders away from the path of good sense will end up among the dead.

**17** Chase pleasure and you'll end up broke. Love luxury and you'll never get ahead.

**18** Sometimes the wicked end up suffering what was meant for the righteous — they become the substitute.

**19** Better to live alone in the desert than with someone who constantly complains and picks fights.

**20** A wise person's home is filled with good things, but a fool burns through everything they have.

**21** Pursue what's right and what's kind, and you'll find life, honor, and integrity.

**22** A wise person can take on a city full of warriors and tear down the defenses they trusted.

**23** Control what you say and you'll save yourself a world of trouble.

**24** The proud, arrogant person — 'mocker' is their name — they act with outrageous self-importance.

**25** Laziness is fatal — the sluggard's own desire kills them because their hands won't do any work.

**26** They spend all day wanting things, but the righteous give freely without hesitation.

**27** The LORD finds the religious offerings of wicked people disgusting — especially when they're offered with evil motives.

**28** A lying witness will be destroyed, but a person who truly listens will have the last word.

**29** A wicked person puts on a tough face, but the upright person carefully considers their path.

**30** No amount of human cleverness, strategy, or planning can overpower the LORD.

**31** You can prepare the horse for battle, but whether you win depends entirely on the LORD.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **21:1**: Stunning image — God steers kings' hearts as easily as a farmer moves water through irrigation ditches. No political power is beyond His influence.

- **21:3**: This is prophetic wisdom — God doesn't want your sacrifices if you're living unjustly. Right living beats religious performance every time.

- **21:31**: The perfect ending to a chapter about sovereignty — prepare all you want, but the outcome belongs to God.

— PNEUMA
